summary: Inspected ownership, organization membership, create/update transitions, server-owned writes, types, private attachments and read scopes. Repository rules/workflow suite passes 153 tests. No tested cross-organization or role escalation bypass found. Score is not a guarantee and does not cover every production identity or payload.

findings.issue: Some legacy text fields, including equipment name/location/note, validate type and ownership but lack application-specific upper bounds. Authorized writers can create unusually large legitimate documents up to Firestore limits.
findings.recommendation: Inventory existing lengths, add compatible per-field bounds for creates/changed values and regression tests. Preserve existing long records during rollout; do not treat the database document size limit as an application quota.

findings.issue: Published rules intentionally omit unreleased center dispatch access present in the repository. A blanket rules deploy would change that scope.
findings.recommendation: Keep the center rollout gated and verify the exact published rules separately. No rules deployment is part of this UI audit.

findings.issue: Read-only production inspection found no backup schedules, PITR disabled and database deletion protection disabled. Access rules alone do not protect against mistaken privileged operations.
findings.recommendation: Obtain approval for the proposed daily seven-day backup policy and deletion protection, verify the first completed backup, and rehearse restore into a separate database. Include Auth and Storage in a separate recovery plan.
